transcripts.transcript:
Good afternoon, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How may I help you?

Hello, Rachel. It's Adrian Lim. I'm on a break at work and have my investment notes here. My identification number is T eight three three one seven two five K. My date of birth is 29 December 1987.

Thank you, Adrian. We can keep the conversation focused. Have you settled back into your regular work routine?

Mostly, yes. My diary is more predictable again, although there is still plenty to catch up on. The fund I want to transact in is Harbor SGD Bond Fund.

I'll give you a moment to check your notes before we continue.

Sorry, I was looking at the wrong part of my notes. Replace that selection with Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund.

Take your time. There is no need to rush through the page while we're speaking.

Actually, I've found the relevant entry now: I meant Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund. Cancel my earlier fund selections; this is my final choice.

Your objective is to diversify your income-oriented portfolio with emerging-market bond exposure, holding it over the longer term despite fluctuations. For Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, rising interest rates can reduce the market value of the bonds held by the fund. Are you willing to accept investment losses on this allocation?

Yes, I am willing to accept investment losses on this allocation. I want to keep it bounded rather than change my whole portfolio.

Before we move on, is there anything about the format of your routine portfolio updates that you would like us to note?

Please keep them concise, with clear headings. I tend to read them between appointments, and a long narrative is difficult to work through. I can ask for more detail when I need it.

I'll note that presentation preference for routine updates. I recommend Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund because its emerging-market bond exposure supports your aim of diversifying your income-oriented investments. Keeping the allocation bounded also fits your preference for measured risk.

Thank you for setting that out. I've now got the rest of my notes in front of me, rather than the loose pages I started with.

There is also the transaction charge to cover. The transaction fee is 0.5% of the transaction amount.

The transaction currency should be Singapore dollars. The amount I am committing to this transaction is 25,000. My planning notes also show 100,000 Singapore dollars, but that was only an illustrative allocation, not an instruction to invest that amount. For context, my overall account value is 1,200,000 Singapore dollars. That's the account total, not the amount for this transaction. The quantity for my order is 100 units. To be clear about the direction, I want to buy. Please use a limit order with a limit price of 250 Singapore dollars per unit.

Please confirm your final instruction: buy 100 units of Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, with an allocation of 25,000 Singapore dollars, using a limit order at a limit price of 250 Singapore dollars per unit. Shall I proceed on that basis?

Yes, I confirm that final instruction exactly as you stated it. Please proceed with the order.

Thank you, Adrian. Please look out for the usual order documentation through your established correspondence channel. I'll let you get back to work.

Thank you, Rachel. That was helpful. Goodbye.
